hits.description:
Session serializer mismatch can lead to remote code execution.

hits.description:
Partially overwritten session files can lead to remote code execution.

The files session save handler, which is the default, writes updated session data into the existing session file without first clearing it. If a write is interrupted, the file can contain the beginning of the new session followed by the end of the old one, and bytes of an ordinary string can later be unserialized as objects. hits.description:

hits.description:
Use-after-free in magic method backtraces can lead to remote code execution.

hits.description:
Timezone cache use-after-free can lead to remote code execution.

hits.title: PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free can lead to local privilege escalation
hits.description:
PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free can lead to local privilege escalation.

When catch_workers_output is enabled and the epoll event backend is used, the PHP-FPM master can close a worker's output pipe in fpm_child_close() without removing the associated event, and the delayed cleanup can free the worker record while its epoll registration is still active. hits.description:
Denial of service through folded HTTP response headers.

The HTTP stream wrapper joins each continuation line of a folded response header to the accumulated value by allocating a new string and copying the whole value, so a response with many short continuation lines takes disproportionate CPU time to parse. hits.description:
Mixed-case HTTPS and FTPS URLs can expose data in plaintext.

The HTTP and FTP stream wrappers recognise URL schemes case-insensitively, but enable TLS only when the scheme contains a lowercase "s" at a fixed position. hits.description:
PHAR OpenSSL signature bypass via algorithm downgrade.

The Phar extension selects the signature verification method from the signature type stored in the archive, and only the OpenSSL types consult the separate .pubkey file holding the trusted public key.
